title: Infosys Becomes World's First Organization Assessed at CMMI AI Maturity Level 5
excerpt: An assessment by Benchmarked Pty Ltd, a CMMI Institute licensed partner, sampled Infosys projects from a pool of more than 1,000 across service lines and geographies — and placed the Bengaluru-headquartered company at the AI maturity model's highest level.
body:
• Infosys has become the world's first organization assessed at Maturity Level 5 of the CMMI AI Maturity (AIM) Model, the model's highest level, the company announced on November 25, 2026.
  • The assessment, conducted by Benchmarked Pty Ltd, a licensed partner of the CMMI Institute, sampled projects from a pool of more than 1,000 across Infosys service lines, geographies and independent functions.
  • For clients, the rating is a governance signal: Infosys says the assessment evaluated how AI is governed, deployed and measured across its global delivery environment, including responsible AI controls.
  • Infosys (NSE: INFY, BSE: INFY, NYSE: INFY) employs more than 325,000 people and operates in 59 countries.

Infosys has become the world's first organization to be assessed at Maturity Level 5 of the CMMI AI Maturity (AIM) Model, the company announced on November 25, 2026. The assessment was conducted by Benchmarked Pty Ltd, a licensed partner of the CMMI Institute, an ISACA enterprise. Level 5 is the highest level in the model, which assesses how organizations govern, deploy and measure artificial intelligence in their operations.

The recognition follows Infosys's participation in the CMMI AI Maturity (AIM) pilot assessment. The Level 5 assessment covered a broad array of projects across service lines, geographies and independent functions globally, sampling from more than 1,000 projects, according to the company. It evaluated how AI is governed, deployed and measured across Infosys's global delivery environment, and its impact on overall performance and client outcomes.

What the assessment examined

According to Infosys, the assessment recognized the company's focus on adopting mature AI practices and integrating responsible AI governance and risk management into the software engineering lifecycle through the use of AI tools and platforms. It also confirmed, the company said, that Infosys has achieved statistically validated business performance gains from CMMI AIM-guided processes incorporating AI solutions and technologies.

Infosys said it has delivered consistent and predictable outcomes within time and budget, reflected in accelerated productivity improvement, faster release cycles and time-to-market, improved business performance and reduced total cost of ownership. The company links that delivery record to its AI-first offering, Infosys Topaz, together with its Responsible AI Office, AI centers of excellence and governance mechanisms, which it uses to operationalize AI across service delivery and internal business processes.

"We are immensely proud to be the world's first organization to achieve the highest level of CMMI AI Maturity (AIM)."

— Dinesh Rao, Executive Vice President and Chief Delivery Officer, Infosys

Dinesh Rao, Executive Vice President and Chief Delivery Officer at Infosys, said the recognition reflected how the company has embedded AI across its operations, combining engineering discipline with responsible governance and continuous improvement. Chris Dimitriadis, Chief Global Strategy Officer at ISACA, congratulated the Infosys team and said the result showed how responsible governance, disciplined innovation and continuous improvement can translate AI ambition into measurable business value.

Why it matters

Coverage of the announcement by IT Brief noted that Level 5 is the model's top rating, intended to reflect a high degree of process control and continuous improvement in the use of AI. For enterprise clients choosing an AI services provider, an independently assessed maturity rating offers a comparison point that marketing claims do not: the assessment sampled real delivery projects rather than a single showcase engagement.

Infosys describes itself as a global leader in AI-first business consulting and technology services, with more than 325,000 people working across 59 countries and more than four decades of experience managing the systems of global enterprises. The company said it does not undertake to update forward-looking statements in the release except as required by law.
